## Is this a BUG / ISSUE report or a QUESTION?

#### Hardware / network configuration, and filesystems used.
All communication taking place on LAN, ext4 filesystem on server and client. BORG connections being made over ssh using authorized keys.

#### How much data is handled by borg?
~150GB

#### Full borg commandline that lead to the problem (leave away excludes and passwords)
```
borg list borg@participant4:/srv/nfs/backups/borg/laptop-e5440
```

## Describe the problem you're observing.
Cannot list any contents for encrypted repositories (encrypted with RSA KEY and passphrase), but CAN list contents for unencrypted repos.  I suspect this could be a problem with msgpack version.  Stacktrace below.

BORG environment variables are set correctly, and were verified multiple times:
```

BORG_RSH=ssh -i /home/<user>/.ssh/borg-at-arch-bees
BORG_KEY_FILE=/home/<user>/.config/borg/keys/arch_bees__srv_nfs_backups_borg_laptop-e5440
```

#### Can you reproduce the problem? If so, describe how. If not, describe troubleshooting steps you took before opening the issue.
Yes, can reproduce every time, using any command (not just list command) against an encrypted repo.  I also tried temporarily moving the integrity file out of the repo area, but got the same stacktrace.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Borg does not use RSA keys.

Also, one does not usually need to use `BORG_KEY_FILE`, but if one does, one must make very sure it points to the correct key file depending on the repo.

Maybe try `BORG_PASSPHRASE` rather than `BORG_PASSCOMMAND` and make sure it contains the correct passphrase.

Did you use `export` to actually have these variables **in the borg process environment**?

Did you check the contents of the `arch_bees__srv_nfs_backups_borg_laptop-e5440` file and whether it is readable?

I am not aware of any msgpack problems in recent times.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
I'd try to establish a test base from a segregated env like a container or a live USB, possibly once from both ends. Then we know, if it's a version mismatch, and if any combos work.

I see you use arch (= life on git master), try e.g. a Debian stable that we know works for sure. Even, if you understandably don't want docker on the desktop, you could install it, `docker run --rm -it debian bash`, then purge after. There are also specific python images like `python:3.11` to see if there's any difference. (Don't think so, though, or there'd be a million posts.)

Docker containers use the host kernel, but I wouldn't expect the kernel to make a difference.

But a version issue seems odd as the python packages should be identical, and msgpack only has a minor diff. Crypto is usually very backwards compatible so any system lib mismatch there also seems unlikely to cause trouble even if you're on the very latest.

Getting a working base and then finding differences seems most useful either way, unless anyone has a direct clue. Quick enough with borg's init/create/list.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Had a look into borg 1.2.4 source code:

Considering it ran into `borg.crypto.key:590` (in **both** of your tracebacks), it means that it did **not** get a passphrase from the environment (neither via BORG_PASSPHRASE, nor via BORG_PASSCOMMAND, nor via BORG_PASSPHRASE_FD).

It then finds the key like:
- check BORG_KEY_FILE in env and if it is there, use that path for the keyfile
- otherwise, try to find the key in the keys directory (trying all files there until one passes the sanity check)
- in both cases, it does a sanity check on the keyfile (whether it starts with BORG_KEY REPOID).

It then tries to load the found key:
- first it tries an empty passphrase (*)
- if that doesn't work, it asks 3 times for the passphrase and retries with the entered values

(*) As it fails there already with "no more data to unpack", it looks like the key file it found and read data from was empty (except the BORG_KEY REPOID) or corrupted.

@participant1 thanks for all of the great info.  I have some updates and observations:

I was able to create a brand new repo with key and passphrase, and everything worked as expected, i.e. `borg list` completed without error.  This was performed on the same machines (no virtual or isolated environment was created).

With the test repo that doesn't have issues, I was getting prompted for the repo password at the command line as expected.  With the problematic repo, I never get prompted for the password on the command line. If I fail to supply the env var `BORG_PASSPHRASE`, execution passes through
```
/usr/lib/python3.11/site-packages/borg/crypto/key.py", line 590
```
If I supply the correct BORG_PASSPHRASE value as an env var, execution passes through 
```
/usr/lib/python3.11/site-packages/borg/crypto/key.py", line 598
```

What may be the most interesting thing is running
```
borg key export borg@participant4:/srv/nfs/backups/borg/laptop-e5440
```
against the problematic repo.  That results in a successful response:
```
BORG_KEY c486baae3axxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```
If I then attempt to use this key with `borg list`, I get the same msgpack error.

The data in these repos is pretty important to me, and it's actually the only spot I can access it thanks to the hard drive that was housing it reaching end-of-life. That hard drive is now completely dead. Are there any alternative methods of getting the data decrypted given that I have both the correct key and passphrase?

It looks like the key file it "found" does not contain an encrypted key.
It might have a line 1 like `BORG_KEY <REPOID>`, but some base64 encoded encrypted key should be in line 2+.

Maybe put a `print(target)` before line 598, so you see what filename it is using.


comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
The first line **must only** have `BORG_KEY <REPOID>` (`<REPOID>` is 256bits == 64 hex digits).
The encrypted key **must be in line 2+**.

Maybe the encrypted key must not be split in several lines as in my example, that is just how borg 1.2.4 generated it on my machine / using my python. But IIRC the base64 decoder can tolerate white space differences.

comments.author: participant1

# enhancement idea

`sanity_check` method only checks `BORG_KEY <REPOID>`, but not the `\n` after that nor that line 2+ contains something base64.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
It was the absence of newlines in the key file! When I created the repo originally I copied the output of the keyfile into my password manager. That operation somehow managed to lump both lines together. I am not sure if that was due to how Borg outputs the key file data or if it was a mistake on my part (it was a while ago).

My notes in my pw manager state: `(all text below should be provided as a SINGLE LINE)` so at the time I clearly believed the keyfile was a one-liner which is not the case.

I am able to access my data now having split the keyfile between the repo id the key below using a newline char.

For those who might have this issue in the future, you can verify what your repo id is by going to the server and looking at the contents of the `config` file, e.g.:
